tfidf_matching.interpretation: TF-IDF correctly matched 3 out of 10 resumes to their correct job descriptions. Relies heavily on keyword frequency, which can miss semantic meaning.

key_findings: TF-IDF baseline achieved 30% accuracy on realistic resume-JD matching
Exact keyword matching has limitations with semantic understanding
Multiple resumes contain overlapping keywords (Python, AWS, Docker, etc.) causing confusion
Resume 0 (Python), 4 (DevOps), 9 (Systems Admin) had distinctive enough keywords to match correctly
Resumes 1-3, 5-8 had keyword overlap causing incorrect matches
This demonstrates why semantic matching (Sentence-BERT) is needed for better accuracy
recommendations: Use semantic embeddings (Sentence-BERT) to improve beyond 30% accuracy
Combine keyword matching with semantic similarity for better results
Larger evaluation set (100+ resume-JD pairs) would provide more robust metrics
